source: CARDI book "ដំណាំស្រូវនៅកម្ពុជា" (Rice Cultivation in Cambodia), by Men Sarom, Thuy Lina and Pheng Thimuny, published by CARDI, 2007, Chapter 2 (Rice-growing environment), by Preap Visarto, section 2.4 (Water). No elibrary URL visible.
text: Rice water requirement is measured mainly through transpiration (water lost through the plant to the atmosphere), which the source distinguishes from soil-surface evaporation. A comparison table in the source (Table 2.1) gives transpiration ratio - grams of water transpired per gram of dry matter produced - by growth stage for indica versus japonica rice: at the seedling stage, indica requires about 395 g water/g dry matter versus 240 for japonica; at tillering, about 497 for indica versus 238 for japonica; at the reproductive stage, about 633 for indica versus 242 for japonica; giving an overall average of about 520 for indica versus 240 for japonica. This indicates japonica rice is notably more water-efficient than indica across all growth stages in this comparison. Separately, a whole-crop water-requirement table (Table 2.2) breaks down total water needed per hectare (in mm depth, encompassing a roughly 21-day nursery period plus the main field period) by stage: about 262mm at the seedling stage, 332mm at tillering, and 407mm at the reproductive stage, for an estimated total crop water requirement in the range of 250-400mm depth (equivalent to roughly 2,500-4,000 tons of water per hectare) across the full growth cycle. The reproductive stage - particularly the panicle-initiation/booting window - is identified as the most drought-sensitive period; the source indicates soil moisture should be maintained at a high level (in the range of roughly 50-70% of saturation/field capacity is implied by the surrounding discussion) during this window, and that moisture stress at this stage can reduce yield by up to around 40%.
caveat: The two source tables (2.1 and 2.2) are dense and were read via page rasterization; the transpiration-ratio and stage-water-requirement figures above are transcribed as given in the source, but should be treated as illustrative rather than precision-guaranteed given the general difficulty of reading dense tabular data this way. A separate figure in the source (correlating grain yield with daily transpiration rate, R=0.88) was not transcribed since it is a scatter-plot relationship rather than a lookup value. Recommend a duplicate-check against any existing water-management or AWD (alternate wetting and drying) content once repo access is available.
